item.title: Fijiana 7s fine-tune preparations ahead of Dubai 7s
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 23/11/2026 The Fiji Airways Fijiana 7s side are fine-tuning their preparations ahead of the HSBC SVNS Dubai 7s this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 23/11/2026

The Fiji Airways Fijiana 7s side are fine-tuning their preparations ahead of the HSBC SVNS Dubai 7s this weekend.

The side is focusing on strength, recovery and team spirit as the players look forward to another challenging tournament.

The team hit the gym shortly after arriving in Dubai, and their focus remains on the upcoming tournament.

Last year, the side finished fourth at the Dubai 7s after losing 22-12 to Japan.

The Fijiana will kick off their campaign against Canada at 6.44pm on Saturday. They will then take on Japan at 11.44pm before playing New Zealand at 2.52am on Sunday in their final pool match.

The women's semi-finals will begin at 9.12pm on Sunday, while the final is scheduled for 3.35am next Monday.

Meanwhile, the Fiji Men's 7s team will meet New Zealand in their first pool match at 8.36pm on Saturday. They will then take on France at 11.17pm before facing Spain at 4am on Sunday in their final pool match.

The men's semi-finals will kick off at 10.06pm on Sunday, while the final is scheduled for 4.11am next Monday.

Reddy and McGechan crowned Mr and Ms Fiji 2026
item.description: Zynal Reddy and Charlene McGechan have been crowned Mr and Ms Fiji 2026, with McGechan also winning three categories, including the Transformation Category after losing 20.2 kilograms. The Fiji Bodybuilding and Fitness Federation held the Mr and Ms Fiji 2026 National Bodybuilding Championship at the Grand Pacific Hotel in Suva on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Zynal Reddy and Charlene McGechan have been crowned Mr and Ms Fiji 2026, with McGechan also winning three categories, including the Transformation Category after losing 20.2 kilograms.

The Fiji Bodybuilding and Fitness Federation held the Mr and Ms Fiji 2026 National Bodybuilding Championship at the Grand Pacific Hotel in Suva on Saturday.

Reddy secured the Men’s Open Bodybuilding Under 85kg title before being named the overall Mr Fiji 2026.

McGechan had an outstanding night, winning the Women’s Bikini, Women’s Figure and Transformation categories before taking home the Ms Fiji 2026 title.

Her 20.2-kilogram weight loss and lifestyle transformation highlighted the importance of discipline, consistency, improved health and confidence.

The championship also recognised athletes across several other categories.

Gibran Sahukhan won both the Men’s Physique and Men’s Classic Physique titles, while Rajnesh Rishi Raj took out the Men’s Masters Bodybuilding and Men’s Open Bodybuilding Under 70kg categories.

Other winners included Beverly Palliser in the Women’s Gym Model category, Param Shivam in the Men’s Open Under 65kg, Delpreet Singh in the Under 75kg, Neles Chand in the Under 80kg and William Robert in the Under 90kg category.

Another significant moment of the evening was the presentation of the inaugural Jekesoni “Superman” Yanuyanudrua Award to Nilesh Chand.

The award was established in memory of the late Jekesoni Yanuyanudrua and recognises qualities such as dedication, commitment, discipline, stage presence, sportsmanship, humility and resilience.

Jekesoni’s father also joined the presentation in honour of his son's legacy.

The Federation says the Transformation Category was an important part of this year's championship as it recognises that bodybuilding and fitness are not just about physical appearance, but also about improving health, confidence and making positive lifestyle changes.

The Federation also acknowledged the athletes, coaches, families, officials, judges, volunteers and supporters who contributed to the successful event.

It also thanked its sponsors, including NEWWORLD IGA, FINTEL, SCAFF and SCAFF (FIJI) PTE LTD, ALL FREIGHT LOGISTICS, PRIME PHARMACY, VINOD PATEL, Imtiaz Sahukhan and SHIVZ INVESTMENT.

Looking ahead, Reddy says he wants to help grow bodybuilding in Fiji and ensure the sport receives greater recognition.

McGechan is also encouraging more women to take up fitness, saying the journey can help build confidence and develop a positive mindset.

The Federation says it will continue creating opportunities for athletes, encouraging greater participation among women and making the sport accessible to more people in Fiji.
